verified_against_binary: v2.36.6 implements Fix F from the content-pass plan, which had been planned in two revisions and never built: the site pointed at neither of the two tools it was supposed to. Placement is by READER MOMENT rather than by category, because the two tools answer different questions. skill-creator-plus is for someone who has not written the skill yet, so it sits at the entry point; cowork-harness answers 'does mine do this?', which every rule on the site provokes and the site previously left unanswered, so it sits where a reader has just finished the rules -- the index and the contract page. Neither appears on a topic page, where it would compete with that page's 'What is not established' section, and neither is in the footer. Headings follow the moment: 'Where this fits in your workflow' at the entry point, 'Checking your own skill against these' after 52 rules. Per the plan's own rev-2 correction the blurbs are DATA (a validated `tools` array in author-facts.json), not hand-written template strings, and they are explicitly not findings: no tier badge, no verified date, and same-author disclosure on every rendering. Three tests pin the placement (both at the entry point, harness only on the contract page, neither on any topic page), the no-tier-badge rule, and md/HTML parity.
note: The tools array is validated for shape and https-absolute URLs but deliberately carries no tier or verified date: it is a pointer, not a claim about product behaviour, and mixing the two would erode the tier discipline the rest of the site depends on.
